audit_findings.title: Borrower-defense recoupment is a potentially unreserved claim ahead of equity
audit_findings.magnitude: $1.4 million of discharged loans for 280 borrowers is filed; exposure across approximately 3,000 claims is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Any recoupment would reduce cash through the equity bridge or reduce future owner earnings if paid from operations.
audit_findings.evidence: The DOE may attempt to impose liability on the Company for reimbursement for the discharged loans.
audit_findings.explanation: The filed $1.4 million alone is only 0.5% of the $272 million base equity value and would not change the conclusion. However, the company says some of approximately 3,000 claims may already have been discharged and DOE could seek reimbursement. The record establishes a contingent exposure but not a probable liability, accrual error, or total amount, so materiality remains unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Obtain DOE claim and discharge data, subsequent correspondence, the accounting contingency memorandum, any accrual, insurance or indemnification, and rerun the bridge with low, central, and full-recoupment amounts supported by that evidence.

audit_findings.title: Committed expansion spending may make the FY2025 owner-earnings anchor non-repeatable
audit_findings.magnitude: $86.633 million FY2025 capital expenditures, equal to 5.35x the $16.2 million anchor; $29.132 million H1 2026 capital expenditures, equal to 1.80x the anchor; unavoidable portion unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Any committed or maintenance-like spending excluded as discretionary growth investment must reduce the owner-earnings anchor or the corresponding near-term projected owner earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: Capital expenditures were 16.7% of revenues in 2025 and are expected to be approximately 12.1% of revenues in 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: This is not yet a demonstrated classification error because the owner-earnings reconciliation is absent. Nevertheless, actual spending dwarfs the anchor, the company expected 2026 capital expenditures of approximately 12.1% of revenue, and Hicksville and Rowlett were already contractually underway. Even a modest unavoidable portion could materially reduce the $16.2 million starting cash flow and all scenario values.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile FY2025 owner earnings line by line to the $86.633 million capital expenditures, then map committed 2026-2027 buildout, equipment, tenant-improvement and startup cash requirements by campus. Rerun every scenario after deducting the evidenced unavoidable portion.

audit_findings.title: The latest debt burden may not be represented in the FY2025 earnings numerator
audit_findings.magnitude: $26.0 million revolver debt plus $30.898 million finance-lease liabilities at June 30, 2026; H1 2026 interest expense was $1.895 million versus $1.514 million in H1 2025; ongoing incremental run-rate is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Because this is an equity-level owner-earnings model, ongoing interest and facility fees must reduce projected owner earnings rather than principal being deducted again in the bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, the Company had no debt outstanding under the Facility.
audit_findings.explanation: The date mismatch is demonstrated: the $16.2 million anchor comes from FY2025, while $26.0 million of revolver debt existed at June 2026. Finance-lease interest was already present in FY2025, and the filed half-year increase in total interest expense is only $0.381 million, or 2.4% of the anchor. Because the June balance was not outstanding for a full comparable period, the current run-rate effect cannot be established from the supplied record.
audit_findings.action: Separate revolver and finance-lease interest in the FY2025 owner-earnings reconciliation, obtain monthly 2026 debt balances, rates and fees, calculate a current annualized interest burden, and rerun the OE scenarios from the first projection year.

audit_findings.title: Gross cash may not all be distributable excess cash
audit_findings.magnitude: $44.178 million gross cash added versus $51.920 million unearned tuition; challenged bridge amount up to $44.178 million, equal to 16.2% of the $272 million base equity value and approximately $1.37 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Only excess cash belongs in the equity bridge; cash required for advance-tuition obligations, Title IV administration, collateral or minimum operating liquidity must remain with the operating business.
audit_findings.evidence: Unearned tuition represents contract liabilities primarily related to our tuition revenue.
audit_findings.explanation: The valuation demonstrably adds the entire cash balance, while filed unearned tuition exceeds that cash balance. Unearned tuition is not automatically a dollar-for-dollar restriction, so the record does not prove that none of the cash is excess. The challenged amount is nevertheless large enough to materially change each scenario value and therefore cannot remain unsupported.
audit_findings.action: Determine the June 2026 composition of cash, segregated Title IV balances, unearned-tuition funding needs, restricted or collateralized amounts and minimum operating liquidity. Rerun the bridge using only cash affirmatively demonstrated to be excess.

audit_findings.title: The fully diluted share count is not demonstrated to be a true ceiling
audit_findings.magnitude: 0.613476 million shares separate the 31.721479 million August cover count from the 32.334955 million valuation count, equal to 1.90%; total FY2025 grants were 0.395383 million shares, equal to 1.22% of valuation shares
audit_findings.mechanism: Double-counting issued restricted shares overstates the denominator and understates value per share, while omitted above-target performance shares understate the denominator and overstate value per share.
audit_findings.evidence: Under such grants, no shares vest in the event that less than 80 % of the target is achieved; vesting begins at 25 % for 80 % achievement and increase on a linear scale up to 200 % vesting for achievement of 120 % or more of the target.
audit_findings.explanation: The supplied numbers strongly indicate that the valuation added the June 2026 nonvested balance to the later cover-page outstanding count, but an award-level reconciliation is required to prove double counting and capture maximum performance payouts. The known quantities are low-single-digit percentages of the denominator: a 1.90% denominator difference changes the $8.41 base value by only about $0.16 per share, while even all FY2025 grants are only 1.22% of the valuation denominator. Neither scale could change the conclusion relative to the $25.64 market price.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile each award to legally outstanding shares, remove awards already included in the cover count, add only incremental shares at maximum payout, and update per-share outputs without changing enterprise or equity values.

audit_findings.title: The latest anchor may retain a nonrecurring pension termination charge
audit_findings.magnitude: $0.926 million pre-tax charge, equal to 5.7% of the $16.2 million anchor; full pre-tax reversal would add approximately $13.0 million to base operating PV and approximately $0.40 per share before consistent tax and receipt treatment
audit_findings.mechanism: Removing a nonrecurring charge would increase normalized owner earnings, but any surplus receipt and related tax effects must also be removed or normalized consistently.
audit_findings.evidence: As a result of the plan termination, the Company received a reversion of excess plan assets of approximately $1.9 million subject to a 50% federal excise tax, which resulted in pension excise tax expense of $0.9 million, recorded in other expense.
audit_findings.explanation: Retention in the anchor is possible but not demonstrated because the owner-earnings reconciliation is missing. Even the conservative upper-bound calculation that reverses the entire charge raises base value only from approximately $8.41 to $8.81 per share before tax and receipt consistency, still far below the $25.64 price. It therefore cannot change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Inspect the FY2025 owner-earnings reconciliation for the $1.9 million surplus reversion, $0.926 million excise tax, settlement amounts and associated income-tax effects; normalize all related nonrecurring items symmetrically and update the scenarios.
